title: [Performance]: Avoidable preemption at hybrid Attention/Mamba decode block transitions (vLLM #62752)
quote: Allocation fails and request `6` is preempted.
proves: CPU reproducer with real AsyncScheduler: 7 running hybrid requests, 5 spec tokens + 5 lookahead slots, 148-block pool; unmodified scheduler preempts, a reordering that leaves headroom for Mamba state-boundary blocks completes all 7 without preemption at the same pool size. Opened 2026-10-20.
does_not_prove: Simulated outputs, no kernel or serving; the avoidable preemption is caused by Mamba state-block transitions under FCFS ordering, not by lookahead slots alone; no goodput numbers.
bearing: C1: the only live 'avoidable preemption with spec' report is hybrid-model state blocks, already being addressed upstream; scoop for any hybrid variant of C1.

title: fix(v1): prevent IMA after speculative preemption (vLLM PR #49620)
quote: a request can be preempted after a speculative decode frame has been dispatched but before its output returns
proves: Under async scheduling a preempted request's in-flight spec frame becomes stale; fix discards stale output with a budget in placeholder-token units of 1 + num_scheduled_spec per frame. Open since 2026-07-23.
does_not_prove: Correctness fix only; no cost measurement of optimistic scheduling.
bearing: C4: optimism creates rollback/ownership bugs, not a measured goodput cost.

title: [PD] Bootstrap EAGLE draft state on decode after target-only prefill (SGLang PR #40955)
quote: This is an **experimental correctness fallback, not a throughput optimization**: it repeats full-prefix target and draft compute.
proves: Draft-on-D-only placement for EAGLE exists as an opt-in flag: decode replays the committed prefix through target AND draft, because EAGLE needs target hidden states; exposes replay cost as pd_draft_bootstrap_tokens. Open, stacked on #40953.

bearing: C2: 're-prefill only the drafter on D' is not possible for hidden-state drafters; the drafter-only option costs a full target replay.

title: DFlash (arXiv 2602.06036v2)
quote: We treat the fused target context feature as persistent contextual information and directly inject it
proves: DFlash fuses 5 target hidden states through a lightweight projection, then injects the fused feature into the K and V projections of every draft layer; 5 draft layers (8 for Qwen3 Coder). So draft context KV is a projection of one fused feature per token, not a full drafter forward over the prompt.
does_not_prove: Paper does not discuss PD placement or transfer bytes.
bearing: C2 oracle: DFlash drafter 'prefill' is K/V projections only; shipping the fused feature (8 KiB/token bf16) vs draft KV (20 KiB/token) differs by about 7% of total PD transfer.
